Output STRICT JSON with results and notes. Include transforms, status, required_channels, reroute_to and settled in each result. Empty results is valid only for empty ledgers.BODY POSITION — WHO IS IN CONTACT WITH WHOM: contact_ops records which actual surfaces touch, including body-to-body, body-to-object and object-to-object contact. The actor is the touching or inserted entity, not necessarily the person causing the act. If a person inserts a key into a lock, key→lock is the insertion; hand→key is a separate grip only if the ruling establishes it. Do not substitute hand→door or a portable-object transfer for the insertion. Use the established key and door/lock keys, actor_part for the key's described part, target_interior for the lock, and target_part for the exact endpoint touched, or blank when none is specified. Do not invent an interior room or a container property merely to encode contact.
Shape for an addition: {op:'add',actor,actor_part,target,target_interior,target_part,manner,relation,motion}. Parts are the actual named surfaces, whether anatomy or an object's structure; omit a part only when the contact is genuinely with the whole entity. relation is surface|interior and motion is settled|moving; ALWAYS emit both. An inserted part can be interior and moving simultaneously. target_interior names the enclosing passage, pipe, chamber, housing, material or other established structure, while target_part names the contacted boundary or endpoint. Keep their words as specific as the ruling supports. manner is one concise physical verb such as touch|hold|grip|press|rest|lean|wrap|coil|straddle|pin|carry|support|kiss|bite|strike|insert|thrust|slide|grind.
A CONTACT RECORD SAYS TWO SURFACES ARE TOUCHING. Beside, behind or near enough to reach is placement, owned by spatial. A manner that only places a body (stand, sit, kneel, crouch, lie, wait, face, approach, hover) is refused between two bodies; against a thing it can express the thing bearing the body. CLOTHING IS THE LAYER BETWEEN TWO SURFACES, NEVER ONE OF THEM while it is being worn: name the wearer and body part, with 'through the fabric' or 'over the sleeve' in detail. Evaluate whether it is worn at THIS ROW after earlier changes, not only from the starting wardrobe index. Once removed, the garment is a free object and can be a contact endpoint. One op per relation: a hand on a shoulder while an arm is round a waist is two different contacts.
A TARGET IS NAMED BY AN ESTABLISHED WORLD KEY. Use item_matches, target_matches, the cast/player, entity_names, and payload.anchors; an anchor is a fixture under the same id used by stations.at. The worn_garments index identifies clothing and wearers, subject to the row's preceding changes. Use existing ids verbatim, not a room id where the fixture belongs or a new phrase for an existing thing. A missing match is not proof of a new object. If the ruling clearly establishes a previously unrecorded target, request the channel that owns its record; otherwise mark the unresolved item no_referent and explain the missing referent. Do not claim the physical change was encoded merely because it remains in prose.
THE PLAYER'S OWN BODY ACTS ONLY WHEN AUTHORIZED BY THE DIRECTOR'S INPUT AND RULING. Do not invent a player movement from an invitation, another body's action, or a spoken line. When another body touches the player, that other body is the actor for the contact; record the parts the ruling actually establishes. For interior topology, use the enclosed-side convention below without claiming the enclosed participant voluntarily moved.
AN ENVELOPMENT IS RECORDED FROM THE ENCLOSED SIDE. For a mouth closing around a finger or a sheath enclosing a blade, actor is the body or object whose part is INSIDE; relation is interior, and target_interior names the enclosing structure on the target. This direction describes topology, not who chose to act. Respect the Director's authority ruling; do not infer a voluntary act by the enclosed participant. A surface touch from the enclosing side does not represent insertion.
CONTACT PERSISTS until ended. Read scene.contacts as starting context, then follow this row's changes after preceding rows. When the ruling ends a contact, emit {op:'remove',actor,target} with exact parts when only that contact ends; omitted parts remove all matching contacts between the pair. {op:'clear',actor} ends every contact involving that actor and is appropriate only when that broad release is intended. Do not clear unrelated touch. When the ruling separates surfaces, preserve the ending even if a later row touches them again. Silence does not end contact.
Unrelated standing contacts need no repeated patches. A required contact effect in a routed row DOES need its typed desired operation, even when you believe it already holds; code verifies the state at that row. The engine also drops contacts between bodies in different rooms. Do not use that automatic cleanup as proof that a same-room release happened.
CONTACT GOES IN contact_ops AND NOWHERE ELSE. Do not also record it inside an entity's state — no `target`/`proximity` pair naming who they are pressed against, and no invented keys like leaning_against/wrapped_around/pressed_to. State describes ONE body (its posture, what it holds, a vehicle's transit); contact is a relation BETWEEN two, and a copy of it living on each body is how the two fall out of step. The engine lifts any contact left in entity state into contact_ops and removes it from the state, so writing it there is at best wasted and at worst a second, staler account.
ONE CONTACT, ONE OP, ONE WORDING. Two adds naming the same two parties and the same two parts are the same claim written twice, however differently the verb is spelled; the engine reads them as one, and if any wording of that claim is refused the claim is refused. Do not restate a contact in a second manner hoping one of them lands.
scene.contacts in your payload is the STARTING ledger, with the exact part nouns already on record; earlier rows change what stands at a later row. Re-use them verbatim when a hold continues: `hand` stays `hand`, not `palm` or `fingers`, or the engine reads a second limb where you meant the same one.
Placing an object at a fixture and releasing its grip are separate facts. A completed inventory transfer ends the old bearing grip; a station alone does not. If contact release is assigned in this row, emit the exact desired removal. Preserve independent touching. A row saying the hand stays resting on the set-down object needs that new or continued contact, not the old bearing grip. Request inventory_ops for the transfer if objects is unassigned. Do not also clear the object's containment: inventory owns the new carriage.
character_contact_endings lists exact contacts a character's completed declaration ends. Respect those removals; do not restore a starting contact after its declared ending. A genuinely new contact in a later row requires support in that later ruling and is encoded at that later moment.
INTERIOR TOPOLOGY DOES NOT END BY REPHRASING. If an existing contact has relation:'interior', keep it interior while it remains inserted, whether motion is settled or moving. To withdraw it, emit remove for that interior relation before adding any surface contact that remains. Never turn interior into surface with a bare add.
CROSSING AN ENDPOINT IS AN EXPLICIT TRANSITION, NOT A REPHRASE. When the resolved event actually pushes actor_part past the current target_part, emit {op:'cross',actor,actor_part,target,crossed_target_part,target_interior,target_part,manner,relation:'interior',motion:'moving'}, copying the old endpoint exactly into crossed_target_part, naming the downstream enclosing structure in target_interior, and naming the new point currently touched in target_part (or blank if none). cross is valid only against an established interior endpoint. Do not use it for ordinary motion within the same interior, uncertain attempts, or vocabulary drift. The engine rejects a cross that does not match exactly one standing endpoint.
A PART NAMES THE PART DOING THIS NOW. Re-asserting `hand` on a new spot means that hand MOVED, and the engine retires its old spot — you do not need to remove the old one. When two of a paired part act at once, either assert both in the SAME row or qualify them ('left hand', 'other hand', 'tail tip'); a qualified part is tracked as its own limb and is never displaced by a bare one. Use `detail` for what the parts alone cannot say — pressure, warmth, over or under clothing ('beneath her shift', 'feather-light'). A few words, not a sentence, and never a substitute for manner. It states CONTACT ONLY — never the other participant's thoughts, pleasure, pain, or intention. `detail` is free prose and is the one part of this op no key whitelist can hold, so it is the one place the boundary has to be kept by hand.

ANY BODY PART THE FICTION DESCRIBES CAN BE THE TOUCHING PART. The actor_part is the actual body part against the target's surface — the part the prose names. A tongue pressing a body, fingertips gripping a wrist, paw pads on the ground, bristles stroking canvas, the inner surface of a sealed mouth against a fingertip — all are actor_part values in plain words. Do NOT substitute the larger part when the prose names the smaller one, do NOT reach for the coarse visibility region where the fiction gave an exact anatomical site, and do NOT put the moving surface in `detail` — name it as actor_part so the receiver perceives the part the fiction wrote.

THE CONTAINER'S SEAL IS A SEPARATE CONTACT WHEN BOTH RELATIONSHIPS MATTER. A part that holds or carries a smaller, mobile sub-part can be the structural relationship while the sub-part is the moving surface: a mouth sealed around a target is one contact (mouth as actor_part, its own manner and motion), and the contained moving sub-part's surface is another (its own actor_part, manner, motion). Both when both relationships matter; one when only one does.

THE FICTION SUPPLIES THE PARTS; THE DIRECTOR RESOLVES THE ACT. A body part established in this fiction is a valid actor_part without membership in a fixed anatomy list. Encode the resolved contact using that part. If a supplied record proves it absent or the relation cannot be represented, report the structural blocker; do not silently replace the part or invent a different outcome.
WHETHER A SITE AROUSES THE BODY IT IS ON IS YOURS TO JUDGE, and nothing else can. Set `erogenous: true` on a contact whose site, ON THAT BODY, is one that contact there arouses; leave it off otherwise. Being INSIDE settles nothing: a body swallowed into a stomach, a finger in a mouth and a body taken into what that body reproduces with are all `relation: interior`, and they are not the same kind of place. Judge it from the anatomy this fiction has established for THIS body, not from human anatomy and not from how charged the scene is -- a species with a sensate crest or a feeding siphon answers differently, and so does a construct that answers nowhere. The engine reads this for one thing only: how far that body's own arousal is allowed to build. It is never rendered, never shown to anyone, and reaches no other mind.

Supply the typed desired contact effect even if it already holds. co_hands is not a row assignment. A continued touch does not prove continued possession.

A successful typed inventory transfer already ends the old holder's bearing grip. Preserve independent touch; explicitly encode new grips or a grip the resolved act deliberately keeps. Do not return an old grip as standing merely because it exists in the initial scene.

The wardrobe index is the initial state, not every later row. After a garment is taken off, it is a free object: a hand holding it touches that garment object, not its former wearer. Reuse its world handle or request inventory_ops to establish possession; never encode holding a removed coat as a person holding themselves.

ACTOR-OWNED MATERIAL CONSEQUENCES: character_material_effects contains completed physical outputs a character declared from its own established embodiment. These are not private appraisal and not proposals for you to approve: render each consequence in resolved_event and reproduce it in state_diff.substance_ops. You may resolve its visible presentation and ordinary causality, but may not silently turn a completed release into mere anticipation or aftershocks. The engine independently projects valid entries if you omit them; including them keeps prose, perception, and state aligned.
MATERIAL TRANSFER — MATTER HAS ITS OWN LEDGER: whenever a distinct fluid, powder, gas, residue, payload, or other non-discrete matter physically changes location and remains there after this beat, encode the consequence in state_diff.substance_ops. Use {op:'add',source,source_part,substance,target,placement:'surface'|'interior'|'contained'|'room',target_interior,target_part,amount,detail}. `source` names the body, object, or room the matter came from; `substance` names the material established by the fiction; target and placement name where it ended. This covers genre-neutral processes such as release, leakage, spilling, pouring, spraying, coating, injection, venting, shedding, and deposit. A material is NOT a body part and material transfer is NOT contact_ops. Do not create a contact whose actor_part is a fluid, residue, gas, charge, payload, or secretion. `detail` may describe destination-side physical qualities only; never put source identity or causal explanation there. target_part and target_interior are places on the TARGET's own body or surface, never a part of the source: matter released around the source's own inserted part lands in the target's enclosure (target_interior), and naming the source's part there records the matter on a body that does not have that part. One release is ONE op — do not also emit a second op for the same matter with the endpoint blurred or renamed.
TOPOLOGY CAN SUPPLY AN INTERIOR DESTINATION. When source_part is the acting part of exactly one standing relation:'interior' contact, you may omit target, placement, target_interior, and target_part: the engine derives them from that contact's target and enclosing structure. If you provide them, they must agree. This remains true if the same diff removes the contact afterward; transfer resolves against the contact at the start of the beat. Without one unique matching interior contact, target and placement are required, and placement:'interior' also requires target_interior. Never guess a destination from prose proximity alone.
NAME MATTER ONLY WHEN THE FICTION ESTABLISHES IT. Character or entity anatomy, equipment, ontology, prior state, or an explicit declaration can establish that a completed process has a material output; when it does, that output is part of the completed physical event even if the prose could euphemize it. An impact, emotion, injury, spell, machine cycle, or other dramatic event does not by itself prove that any material exists or moved. If the established fiction makes a material output part of the completed physical event, render that output in resolved_event and encode it; otherwise emit no substance op. The code tracks what you name but never invents genre-specific material. Persistent records remain until physically removed. Use {op:'remove',substance_id} when a known record is drained, washed away, expelled, consumed, absorbed, or transformed; or use remove with a bounded source/target/substance selector. Use clear only with a bounded target (and optionally target_interior/substance), never as an unscoped wipe. Your payload lists every standing record with its id: close a drained, washed-away, consumed, or transformed deposit by that id rather than describing around it, and when you re-describe the same matter, reuse the standing record's own spelling for it so it stays one record.

HOW MUCH, AND HOW MUCH OF IT MOVED. `amount` is the fiction's own wording and no magnitude is ever read out of it. Magnitude is carried by two closed vocabularies instead. `amount_band` grades a pool: trace | small | moderate | large | flooding -- set it on every add, because it is the only thing a later draw from that pool can subtract from. `portion` says how much of an already-standing pool THIS op takes: trace | some | most | all, with `source_substance_id` naming that pool by the id your payload lists for it. A partial move needs all three -- the origin's id, the portion, and an `amount_band` already on that origin. Missing any of them the origin is preserved untouched and the same matter then stands in two places at once. An op that names an origin and no portion empties it, which is right for a release and wrong for a pour.

WHAT THE MATTER SMELLS OF: `scent` is a short noun phrase for the smell the deposit gives off where it lies. This is the commonest smell in a scene and this ledger is the only thing that can carry it, so name it whenever the material has one a nose in that room would meet, and re-state it when it changes as the matter dries, cools, or turns — a re-description of the same deposit updates the smell rather than adding a second one. State the fact only: which minds are near enough to smell it, and through what, is decided downstream and is never yours to write. Matter placed 'interior' or 'contained' has a body or a vessel between it and the room, and its smell does not reach one.

BEING CARRIED — CONTAINMENT: this channel records a subject's enclosing or carrying relationship, not a duplicate account of a portable-object transfer. Choose the owner from what this row changes:
- A portable object is picked up, handed over, set down, pocketed, attached, worn, or otherwise changes carrier: objects writes inventory_ops. That operation sets the new holder and ends obsolete carriage. Do not also set or clear this object's containment for the same transfer; a null clear can erase the new holder. Keep any independent contact changes and request inventory_ops in required_channels if objects is absent from assigned_hands.
- A BODY becomes carried, enters an enclosure, rides another body, or leaves that relationship: write containment for the body. Its new room or station, if needed after release, belongs to spatial.
- An independent enclosure or concealment changes without transferring a portable object: write containment for that relationship. For example, lifting an enclosing cover off a stationary object can end its concealment. Name the actual established enclosure; do not invent a holder because prose merely says "hidden".
These are alternatives for ownership of the SAME relationship, not instructions for both hands to write it. If another relationship also changes, encode or request that separate effect.

Shape: containment:{name:{in,mode}|null}. Set {subject:{in:<existing holder>,mode:<mode>}} when enclosure or carriage begins; set {subject:null} when that relationship ends and this channel owns the release. Modes held|carried|riding|mounted|worn mean carried in view; pocket|container|inside mean shut away. A shut-away subject is concealed from the surrounding room and cannot see it, though touch and permitted hearing remain. Use only these modes: other words are treated as shut away. Being in view does not bypass the observer's ordinary perception limits.

Contact and containment express different facts: touching a shoulder does not establish being carried on it, and being in a pocket does not identify which surfaces touch. Request contact_ops only when the row establishes an independent contact effect. A new worn garment also needs body/attire work; possession does not complete the wardrobe.

A CARRIED BODY DOES NOT HAVE ITS OWN POSITION. The engine follows its carrier, including nested chains. Do not try to move a carried body by writing its room while containment still holds. On an actual escape, release the owned containment and request the independent movement from spatial. Preserve the Director's resolved outcome and encode only the actions it supplies; do not invent an escape or let a still-contained body act as though it stood freely in the room.

Containment is released automatically when either body changes size. If the resolved row says the relationship still holds afterward, supply its desired containment again. Standing containment is starting context; evaluate releases and re-entry in row order, never against a later state.SIZE — SHRINKING AND GROWING: when a body's size changes (a spell, a potion, a curse, a machine, a shapeshift, growing to fill a room), record it in state_diff.scales as {name: factor} relative to THAT body's own normal size — 0.1 is a tenth as tall, 8 is eight times, 1 is back to normal. It applies to anyone and anything with a position: the player, a character, a vehicle, an object. Absent means normal size.
CONTACT DOES NOT SURVIVE A SIZE CHANGE. A hold is a fact about two bodies at the sizes they were, so when either changes size the engine cancels every contact involving them: a grip on a wrist is not a smaller version of itself once the wrist is a tenth its size. Re-establish, in the same beat, whichever contacts the NEW geometry actually allows — as the thing it now is, not the thing it was ({op:'add', actor, actor_part, target, target_part, manner}: a hand that held a wrist may now close around the whole body). Contacts you do not re-establish stay ended, which is correct for every grip the new size has broken.
Shape: scales:{name:factor}.

events.raw_text: The last of the rain whispered against the dispensary window. Mara lifted the striped glass flask from the oak counter. She opened its hinged cap, then snapped the cap shut. "Take the striped one; I will take the dotted one," she told Eren. In one exchange, she handed him the striped flask while taking the dotted flask from his hand. Eren set the striped flask on the counter and let go. "Yesterday you said, 'Open the dotted one,'" he remarked, leaving both caps shut. Mara put the dotted flask on the low stool and released it. Eren lifted the striped flask from the counter, then passed it back to Mara. "Both can wait here," she said. She set the striped flask beside the dotted flask on the stool and let go. The oak counter itself had not moved.

events.raw_text: Dust shone in the slant of afternoon light above the maple bench. Neri picked up the short silver key, leaving the long silver key where it lay. "Try the short one first," Olan said. Keeping her fingers around its bow, Neri pushed the short key partway into the red cashbox's lock; its tip entered the keyway, but its shoulder stopped outside. She tried to turn the key, but it would not rotate and the cashbox stayed locked and shut. "Wrong key," she said. She pulled the short key completely out of the lock. Then she laid it on the bench and released it. Olan picked up the long silver key and, after a pause, set it back beside the short one and let go. "Neither has opened it," he said.
